question: Five hours into a marathon, a runner crosses the line, then grows confused and collapses. What has gone wrong?
answer: Too much water: low blood sodium, or hyponatraemia. Drinking beyond what sweat removes dilutes the blood, and brain cells swell. At the 2002 Boston Marathon 13% of the runners tested had it; weight gain was the strongest warning sign, and slow runners, with hours to drink, were most at risk.
move: A remedy taken just to be safe can be the very thing that hurts.
ask: What do I overdo to be safe without ever checking whether it helps?

clues.text: Headache, vomiting, confusion: she collapses soon after the finish line.
Her temperature is normal, and the day was mild.
On the scale she is 1.5 kg heavier than she was at the start.
She drank a full cup at every station, to be safe.
Blood test: sodium far below normal.

scene.why: A dehydrated runner finishes lighter. Gaining weight means she drank more than she sweated.

reference: Almond et al., Hyponatremia among runners in the Boston Marathon, New England Journal of Medicine 352:1550-1556, 2005, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa043901
